stemBlocks.value: The cross-section of a symmetrical roof is an isosceles triangle. Half the base is b, the vertical height is h, each sloping rafter has length s, and the base angle is θ. a) Express s in terms of b and h. b) Write sin θ + cos θ as a single fraction in terms of b, h and s. c) Given that tan θ = 3/4, show that s = 5b/4. d) Hence find the total length of the two sloping rafters in terms of b.
Think first: The vertical height splits the isosceles triangle into two identical right-angled triangles with legs b and h and hypotenuse s.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p174-q04 from workbook page 174.

contentBlocks.value: The height h is perpendicular to the base, giving legs b and h with hypotenuse s
Result: right angle at the foot of h

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the two ratios at θ and add them.

contentBlocks.value: sin θ = h/s (opposite over hypotenuse), cos θ = b/s (adjacent over hypotenuse)
Result: sin θ + cos θ = (h + b)/s

solutionSteps.instruction: Use tan θ = 3/4 to express h in terms of b.
Substitute into s = √(b² + h²) and double it.

strategyBlocks.value: Work inside one half-triangle: use Pythagoras for s, write the two ratios with respect to θ, then substitute h = 3b/4 from the given tangent.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) s = √(b² + h²)  (b) sin θ + cos θ = (h + b)/s  (c) tan θ = h/b = 3/4 gives h = 3b/4, so s² = b² + 9b²/16 = 25b²/16 and s = 5b/4  (d) total length of the two rafters = 2s = 5b/2

whyThisWorks.value: Symmetry is what makes this work: the perpendicular height of an isosceles triangle bisects the base, creating two congruent right-angled triangles, so one of them carries all the information. Because tan θ fixes the ratio h : b rather than either value, every roof with tan θ = 3/4 is a scaled 3-4-5 triangle, and s always comes out as exactly 5/4 of the half-base.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the full base instead of the half-base b in Pythagoras.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the full base instead of the half-base b in Pythagoras.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing tan θ = b/h instead of h/b — the opposite side is the height.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing tan θ = b/h instead of h/b — the opposite side is the height.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the answer to part d as s rather than 2s, forgetting there are two rafters.

examTip.value: In any isosceles triangle problem, draw the perpendicular height first — it converts the shape into two right-angled triangles you already know how to handle.
